# Data Integrity & Concurrency Checklist: Issues — creation, detail and editing

**Purpose**: Validate that the numbering, invariant, transaction and concurrency requirements in `spec.md` are complete, unambiguous and objectively verifiable, before the feature is decomposed into tasks
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [contracts/mutators.md](../contracts/mutators.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Provenance of the marks below**: every item was evaluated and marked by Claude on 2026-08-31, at the reviewer's explicit instruction to review the checklist, mark what was already true with citations, and apply the recommended fix to the rest. Each item carries its verdict: **Yes** means the requirement already satisfied the criterion and names where; **Fixed** means the specification was changed to satisfy it and names the change. A reviewer who disagrees with a verdict should uncheck that item — the citations are there to be argued with.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

This is a **requirements-quality** review, not a verification pass. Every item asks whether something is *written well*, not whether code *works*.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the constraint that the composite foreign key depends on — a uniqueness guarantee over the project-and-column pair on the referenced table — stated as a requirement, or discovered only at planning? [Gap, Spec §FR-005] — **Fixed**: `FR-005` now requires the uniqueness guarantee over the project-and-column pair, states that a primary key on the column alone does not supply it, and assigns adding it to this feature.
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for the case where a project's issue-counter row is absent when a creation runs? [Gap, Spec §FR-013] — **Fixed**: `FR-066` requires `createIssue` to refuse rather than create one — a fresh counter could reissue a number — with a matching edge case.
- [x] CHK003 Is the shape of the issue-counter row this feature reads specified anywhere a reviewer of R5 would encounter it? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §Key Entities] — **Fixed**: `FR-013` now states what the row must hold, and the new *Obligations this feature places on entries built before it* states it in the form R5's author needs.
- [x] CHK004 Is the base case for the ordering index specified — what value creation writes when the project holds no issue at all? [Gap, Spec §FR-040] — **Fixed**: `FR-040` now requires the first index of the same scheme for an empty project, not an empty or sentinel value.
- [x] CHK005 Is the transaction isolation level, or the guarantee it must provide, stated for any of the three mutators? [Gap, Spec §FR-039, §FR-055, §FR-058] — **Fixed**: `FR-063` prescribes no isolation level and instead fixes the guarantee each transaction must provide, for the counter draw and for `updateIssue`'s read-and-write.
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for what a caller sees when a write is refused by a database constraint rather than by a mutator's own check? [Gap, Spec §FR-050] — **Fixed**: `FR-065` requires a database refusal to reach the caller as the same kind of refusal as any other, in the product's own terms.
- [x] CHK007 Is it specified whether a creation that fails after drawing a number consumes that number or returns it? [Gap, Spec §FR-014] — **Fixed**: `FR-014` now states that a creation which draws a number and then fails does not return it, and that a gap is not an error to correct.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is "the response MUST carry the settled state" defined precisely enough to distinguish a conforming response from a non-conforming one? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-058] — **Fixed**: `FR-058` now defines it: the transaction must have committed before the caller is answered, and no reader on any connection sees an intermediate state.
- [x] CHK009 Is "what each differs from" specified as to form and audience — a value the mutator holds, a value it returns, or a value it records? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-055] — **Fixed**: `FR-055` now fixes all three — determined against the stored values, available where a later entry would write, and **not returned**, because nothing here reads it.
- [x] CHK010 Is the 200-character title bound stated in units a reviewer can apply unambiguously to combining marks, astral-plane characters and emoji? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008] — **Fixed**: `FR-008` now requires both bounds counted the way the database's own `CHECK` counts, which settles the unit question against one authority.
- [x] CHK011 Is it specified whether the length bound applies before or after the trim that `FR-030` requires? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008, §FR-030] — **Fixed**: `FR-008` now requires the bound applied to the value as it will be stored, so the title's is measured after `FR-030`'s trim.
- [x] CHK012 Is "one transaction" stated consistently as one database transaction rather than one logical operation, everywhere the phrase appears? [Clarity, Spec §FR-039, §FR-055, §FR-058] — **Fixed**: `FR-063` fixes it for all three — one transaction in the database's own sense, not one logical operation — and `FR-058` was reworded to match.
- [x] CHK013 Is "under a row lock" specific enough to exclude an implementation that reads and then writes without holding the lock across both? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013] — **Fixed**: `FR-013` now requires the lock held across both the read and the write of its successor, and not released between them.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK014 Do the three mutators' transaction requirements now read alike, or does one still describe its transaction in materially different terms from the other two? [Consistency, Spec §FR-039, §FR-055, §FR-058] — **Fixed**: `FR-063` states the transaction requirement once for all three mutators, so none describes it in different terms.
- [x] CHK015 Are the ordering requirements consistent — does exactly one requirement claim to be the only ordering write in this feature, with no second requirement implying another? [Consistency, Spec §FR-040, §FR-055] — **Yes**: `FR-040` claims sole ordering authorship; `FR-055` denies `updateIssue` any path to the index. No third requirement implies another writer.
- [x] CHK016 Do the immutability requirements agree across every statement of them — project, number, creator and ordering index named identically in each? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-011, §FR-012, §FR-055] — **Yes**: `FR-007`, `FR-011`, `FR-012`, `FR-045` and `FR-055` name the same four immutable fields in the same terms.
- [x] CHK017 Does the cascade requirement agree with the delete-transaction requirement about where the cascade is enforced, with neither implying the mutator body performs it? [Consistency, Spec §FR-057, §FR-058, §FR-059] — **Yes**: `FR-057` puts the cascade in the database, `FR-059` says the arm is the referencing table's declaration, and `FR-058` covers the transaction — none implies the mutator body performs it.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK018 Can "two issues in one project never hold the same number" be objectively verified under concurrency, and does the criterion say what concurrency it must survive? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002] — **Yes**: `SC-002` names concurrent creation as the condition and states both outcomes; `FR-016` and `FR-063` fix the mechanism it must survive.
- [x] CHK019 Is there a measurable criterion for "no caller ever observes a partially deleted issue", stating from what vantage point the observation is made? [Measurability, Spec §SC-011] — **Fixed**: `SC-011` now names the vantage point: any reader on any connection, including one querying the database directly while the delete runs.
- [x] CHK020 Is the no-op-write criterion stated in terms a test can assert without depending on an implementation detail of how the timestamp is written? [Measurability, Spec §SC-018] — **Yes**: `SC-018` asserts against `updated_at`, a data-model fact fixed by §5, not an implementation detail.
- [x] CHK021 Are the structural requirements accompanied by a stated method of verification, given that no user journey observes them? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-001…§FR-008] — **Yes**: The preamble to *Structure and the issue record* fixes the method: the migration for a column's type and bound, and a refused write for a constraint.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are concurrent-edit requirements stated as a requirement rather than only as an assumption and an edge-case bullet, given that no functional requirement or success criterion covers them? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions, §Edge Cases] — **Fixed**: `FR-064` makes last-write-wins a requirement rather than an assumption, and `SC-019` makes it measurable. The assumption bullet was removed as superseded.
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements defined for a column deleted concurrently with a save that moves an issue into it? [Gap, Spec §FR-052] — **Fixed**: `FR-052` now requires such a save refused by the database under `FR-005` and rolled back under `FR-050`, with a matching edge case.
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for the boundary values of each bound — exactly at the limit, and one past it — rather than only for "past its length bound"? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, §FR-037] — **Fixed**: `FR-008` now states both bounds inclusive — exactly at the bound accepted, one more refused — with an edge case naming 200 and 10 000.
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for a due date at the extremes a calendar date admits, or is the accepted range stated as unbounded deliberately? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006] — **Fixed**: `FR-006` now states that every calendar date the type admits is accepted, past dates included, and that no rule refuses one for being early, late or distant.
- [x] CHK026 Is the interaction between deletion and numbering covered by both a requirement and a criterion, rather than by an edge-case bullet alone? [Coverage, Spec §FR-014, §SC-003] — **Yes**: `FR-014` is the requirement, `SC-003` the criterion, US5 scenario 5 the scenario and the edge case the illustration — all four present.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK027 Is the assumption that R5 has already created the counter row for every project stated where this feature depends on it? [Assumption, Spec §Inherited constraints] — **Yes**: *Inherited constraints* states the counter row is R5's and that this feature draws from what `createProject` wrote; the new *Obligations* section states what it must hold.
- [x] CHK028 Is the assumption that persistence tests run against a real database, rather than a mock, stated as a constraint on how these requirements can be satisfied? [Assumption, Spec §Inherited constraints] — **Yes**: *Inherited constraints*, final bullet: database-enforced invariants are tested against a real PostgreSQL instance on a separate database rather than a mock.
- [x] CHK029 Are the cascade arms later entries will attach enumerated precisely enough that each entry's author can identify its own without re-reading §4? [Dependency, Spec §FR-059] — **Fixed**: `FR-059` now names all four arms and their owning entries — comments and activity to R7, label joins to R8, notifications to R11.
